name: es32-base-vertex-and-robustness
title: Base vertex drawing and robustness
summary: Ten quads and two strip quads in ONE vertex buffer, drawn from ONE element array buffer (a single quad pattern as ubyte/ushort/uint plus a strip) with glDrawElementsBaseVertex, glDrawRangeElementsBaseVertex and glDrawElementsInstancedBaseVertex: basevertex selects the mesh, gl_VertexID includes basevertex, instanced attributes ignore it, and the primitive restart index is compared before it is added - all against a CPU model with mutation and GPU negative controls. In a robust context (EGL_CONTEXT_OPENGL_ROBUST_ACCESS + LOSE_CONTEXT_ON_RESET): CONTEXT_FLAG_ROBUST_ACCESS_BIT, glGetGraphicsResetStatus, RESET_NOTIFICATION_STRATEGY, scissor-confined draws whose basevertex points past the buffer end (no error, no reset, later rendering correct), and the bounded queries glReadnPixels / glGetnUniform{f,i,ui}v with canary buffers (exact size, too small, zero, negative).
spec: ES 3.2 §10.5 Drawing Commands Using Vertex Arrays (DrawElementsOneInstance: vertex ID = index + basevertex; DrawElementsBaseVertex, DrawRangeElementsBaseVertex, DrawElementsInstancedBaseVertex; DrawRangeElements errors)
ES 3.2 §10.3.2 Vertex Attribute Divisors (instanced attributes fetched by instance, not shifted by basevertex)
ES 3.2 §10.3.4 Primitive Restart (comparison occurs before the basevertex offset is added)
ES 3.2 §10.3.5 Robust Buffer Access (out-of-bounds vertex fetches: undefined values, no application failure)
ES 3.2 §2.3.1 Errors (implicit sizei rule, ignored commands, untouched pointer outputs, choice among applicable errors)
ES 3.2 §7.12 Shader, Program, and Program Pipeline Queries (GetnUniform*: INVALID_OPERATION if the required size exceeds bufSize)
ES 3.2 §20.2 Pointer, String, and Related Context Queries (CONTEXT_FLAGS, CONTEXT_FLAG_ROBUST_ACCESS_BIT)
ES 3.2 §13.8.2 Scissor Test (confines the out-of-bounds draws)
ES 3.2 appendix E.2 (vertex ID includes basevertex), appendix F.1 (core robust access excludes KHR_robust_buffer_access_behavior)
EGL 1.5 §3.7.1.5 Robust Buffer Access (creation fails if unsupported), §3.7.1.6 Reset Notification Strategy

api.glDrawElementsBaseVertex: meshes 1-3 with UNSIGNED_BYTE / UNSIGNED_SHORT / UNSIGNED_INT indices and basevertex 4/8/12, a gl_VertexID cell, and a TRIANGLE_STRIP with primitive restart (restart compared before basevertex; 254 + 1 = 255 does not restart) - every cell against the CPU model; basevertex 0 equals glDrawElements (mesh 0 appears) and basevertex 8 moves the same call to mesh 2 (pixels); INVALID_VALUE for count -1
api.glDrawRangeElementsBaseVertex: start/end bound the indices before basevertex (start 0, end 3, basevertex 16 and 28) - mesh and gl_VertexID cells against the CPU model; INVALID_VALUE for end < start and count -1, with no drawing (cell (0,7) stays clear)
api.glDrawElementsInstancedBaseVertex: 4 instances of mesh 5 (basevertex 20) whose instanced attribute (offset + tint) is fetched by instance number, not shifted by basevertex, and 2 instances in a gl_VertexID cell - against the CPU model; INVALID_VALUE for instancecount -1
api.glDrawElements: negative control: the same arguments without basevertex draw mesh 0 into the cell the base-vertex scene must leave clear
api.glVertexAttribIPointer: a_index as an integer attribute; gl_VertexID == a_index turns the vertex-ID cells green (pixels)
api.glVertexAttribDivisor: divisor 1 per-instance offset + tint; the 4 instances appear at the predicted cells with the predicted tints
api.glEnable: PRIMITIVE_RESTART_FIXED_INDEX splits the ubyte strip at 255 (both strip quads complete, pixels); SCISSOR_TEST confines the out-of-bounds draws (all other cells match the model)
api.glGetGraphicsResetStatus: NO_ERROR on the healthy robust context, also after the out-of-bounds draws
api.glGetIntegerv: CONTEXT_FLAGS has CONTEXT_FLAG_ROBUST_ACCESS_BIT; RESET_NOTIFICATION_STRATEGY is one of the two §2.3.2 values and equals the requested LOSE_CONTEXT_ON_RESET
api.glReadnPixels: exact bufSize (64 bytes) returns the same bytes as glReadPixels and nothing past bufSize (canary); bufSize 63 and 0 -> INVALID_OPERATION with the buffer untouched; bufSize -1 -> INVALID_VALUE/INVALID_OPERATION with the buffer untouched (XFAIL on Mesa); empty rectangle with bufSize 0 succeeds and writes nothing
api.glGetnUniformfv: vec4 and mat2 (column-major): exact bufSize returns the uploaded values and nothing more, larger bufSize returns exactly 4 values, bufSize - 1 and bufSize = component count -> INVALID_OPERATION, negative -> INVALID_VALUE/INVALID_OPERATION, location -1 -> INVALID_OPERATION; params untouched on every error
api.glGetnUniformuiv: uvec2 including 4000000000u: the same battery (8 bytes)
api.glUniform4f: value read back exactly with glGetnUniformfv
api.glUniform3i: value read back exactly with glGetnUniformiv
api.glUniform2ui: value read back exactly with glGetnUniformuiv
api.glUniformMatrix2fv: column-major mat2 read back exactly with glGetnUniformfv
api.glUniform1i: u_mode switches the scene shader between colour and the gl_VertexID check (pixels)

visual_review.notes: Viewed the 256x256 captures of gpu (radeonsi), llvmpipe and zink (identical): dark blue-grey background with an 8x8 grid of 24 px squares. Top-left cell is empty (mesh 0 never drawn). Second row from the top: blue, orange, light green, yellow (meshes 1-4). Third: four cyan squares darkening left to right (instance tints 1, 3/4, 1/2, 1/4). Fourth: four green squares (gl_VertexID matched everywhere, no red). Fifth: light-blue and pink strip quads, both complete (no missing triangle at the restart). Sixth: one purple square over the robust-access cell, with no stray fragments around it or anywhere else.
